content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Amarillo

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review PMI's specific requirements for your background—whether you hold a bachelor's degree, associate degree, or high school diploma affects the hours of experience you must demonstrate. Gather your project records now.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. Our instructor-led course covers the PMBOK® Guide framework, real-world case studies, and exam-focused strategies. Attend sessions on your schedule from anywhere—no travel required. Upon completion, you'll receive your official 35-hour completion certificate for PMI.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Create your PMI account and submit your formal PMP application, documenting your education and project experience. PMI will audit and verify your credentials. Pay the examination fee at application submission. Allow time for PMI's review process before your exam eligibility window opens.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice exams, study guides, and instructor Q&A sessions—to build confidence. Schedule your computer-based exam through Pearson VUE at a testing center or approved proctored remote location. The PMP exam tests your mastery of project-management domains and situational judgment.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, you'll earn the PMP credential for a three-year cycle. During each renewal period, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, project work, or volunteer service. Before expiration, renew your credential by submitting proof of PDU hours and the renewal fee to PMI.
